subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Edexcel spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Edexcel Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which statement best describes decomposition in computational thinking?
options: Breaking a complex problem down into smaller, more manageable sub-problems
Repeating a block of code a fixed number of times
Removing unnecessary detail to focus on the important information
Storing related data items together under one identifier
questions.explain: Decomposition means breaking a large problem into smaller sub-problems that are easier to solve. Removing unnecessary detail describes abstraction, not decomposition.

questions.q: A programmer designs a login screen and hides how the password is stored and checked behind a single check_password() function. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Abstraction hides complex implementation detail behind a simple interface, so the rest of the program only needs to know what the function does, not how.

questions.q: In Python, which data type would best store the value 3.14?
questions.explain: A float (real) stores numbers with a decimal point such as 3.14. An int stores whole numbers only, str stores text, and bool stores True/False.

questions.q: A program uses the line age = int(input("Enter age: ")). Why is int() used?
options: To validate that the input is inside a sensible range
To round the number to the nearest whole value
To convert (cast) the string returned by input into an integer so arithmetic works
To output the age to the screen
questions.explain: input() always returns a string, so int() casts it to an integer. Without casting, numeric comparisons or arithmetic on the value would fail or behave incorrectly.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a variable and a constant?
options: A variable can only hold numbers; a constant can only hold text
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A constant can change during execution; a variable cannot
A variable's value can change during execution; a constant's value should stay fixed
questions.explain: A variable's stored value can change as the program runs, whereas a constant is a named value intended to remain fixed throughout execution (e.g. VAT = 0.2).

questions.q: In Python, what is the value of 17 % 5?
questions.explain: The % (modulus) operator returns the remainder after division. 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 % 5 = 2. (17 // 5 would give 3, the integer quotient.)

questions.q: Which expression is True when a number x is between 10 and 20 inclusive?
questions.explain: Both conditions must hold, so AND is needed, and inclusive bounds need >= and <=. 'or' would be True for almost any number, and strict > / < would exclude 10 and 20.

questions.q: Which programming construct chooses between different paths of execution based on a condition?
questions.explain: Selection (if / elif / else) chooses a path based on a condition. Sequence runs statements in order, and iteration repeats statements.

questions.q: You must repeat a block of code exactly 10 times. Which is the most appropriate loop in Python?
options: A while loop with no condition
questions.explain: A count-controlled for loop with range(10) is ideal when the number of repetitions is known in advance. A while loop is better suited to condition-controlled repetition.

questions.q: When should a while loop be preferred over a for loop?
options: When the loop should repeat until a condition changes and the count is not known in advance
When you need to store multiple values in one variable
When only one line of code needs to run
When the number of repetitions is fixed and known in advance
questions.explain: A while loop is condition-controlled, so it is preferred when you don't know how many iterations are needed (e.g. keep asking until the user enters valid input).

questions.q: A list is defined as scores = [4, 8, 15, 16, 23]. What does scores[2] evaluate to?
questions.explain: List indexing starts at 0, so scores[0]=4, scores[1]=8, scores[2]=15. A common mistake is treating the index as starting from 1.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of storing data as a record (e.g. name, age, and grade together) rather than in separate unrelated variables?
options: It removes the need for any data types
It makes the program run in binary
It groups related fields about one item together, keeping the data organised
questions.explain: A record groups related fields (of possibly different data types) that describe a single entity, making the data easier to manage than many loose variables.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a function and a procedure?
options: A function returns a value to the caller; a procedure carries out a task without returning a value
A procedure returns a value; a function never does
A function cannot take parameters; a procedure can
There is no difference in Edexcel's specification
questions.explain: A function returns a value (via return) that can be used in an expression, whereas a procedure performs a task (e.g. printing) without returning a value.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a benefit of using subprograms?
options: Code can be reused without rewriting it
The program is easier to read and maintain
It guarantees the program will contain no logic errors
The overall problem is decomposed into smaller parts
questions.explain: Subprograms aid reuse, readability and decomposition, but they do not guarantee correctness - a subprogram can still contain logic errors.

questions.q: If word = "COMPUTER", what does word[0:4] return in Python?
questions.explain: Slicing word[0:4] returns characters at indices 0,1,2,3 (the end index 4 is excluded), giving "COMP". A common mistake is including the character at index 4.

questions.q: Which line correctly joins first = "Ada" and last = "Lovelace" into "Ada Lovelace"?
questions.explain: String concatenation uses the + operator; a space literal " " is added between the two names to produce "Ada Lovelace".

questions.q: In Python, which mode opens a file so that new data is added to the end without deleting existing content?
questions.explain: Append mode "a" adds data to the end of an existing file. Write mode "w" overwrites/clears the file, and read mode "r" only reads.

questions.q: A form checks that a password entered is at least 8 characters long. This is an example of which type of validation check?
questions.explain: A length check verifies the number of characters entered. A range check tests numeric bounds, a type check tests the data type, and a presence check tests that something was entered.

questions.q: Which of these best describes authentication?
options: Checking that input data is sensible and in the correct format
Converting a string into an integer
Confirming the identity of a user, e.g. by username and password
questions.explain: Authentication confirms who a user is (e.g. login credentials). Validation, by contrast, checks that entered data is reasonable and correctly formatted.

questions.q: A trace table is used mainly to:
options: Record how variable values change step-by-step to check an algorithm's logic
Measure how fast the CPU executes instructions
Automatically fix syntax errors in code
questions.explain: A trace table tracks the values of variables at each step as an algorithm executes, helping identify logic errors by comparing expected and actual values.
